director.chapterArc: A revelation of 'Twin-kindled' status followed by a physical breakthrough using the barrow, leading to exhaustion and a new logistical crisis regarding the scarp.
director.restraintNote: The narrator must maintain Callie's internal arithmetic rhythm during the husk count (P0002-P0003) but shift to breathless physicality when describing the cold and numbness. The revelation of 'Twin-kindled' requires flat, factual delivery from Katori, not melodrama. The barrow sequence must feel mechanical and heavy, emphasizing the transfer of weight rather than magic.

cues.delivery: Rhythmic, counting-like internal monologue. Precise articulation of numbers.
cues.from: By first light the cold had reached the middle of her chest, and she had stopped being able to spit.
cues.through: Callie knew both facts the way she knew the count, which was twenty-six. She had killed or tipped twenty-six since the causeway. They had come in ones all night, from the gravel, from the ditch on the east side of the road, and once from the flats behind, and every one of them had come round the corner of the pump house straight to the doorway where she sat. Not one of them had looked at the walls. Not one had tried the windows. They came to her the way water finds the lowest place in a field, and she stood up and met each one in the road and put it down, and came back and sat on the sill.
cues.reason: Establishes Callie's hyper-analytical state and physical exhaustion.

cues.delivery: Staccato rhythm for the failed pull; quiet relief when Katori intervenes.
cues.from: Somewhere around the twentieth she had stopped being able to feel her feet. Somewhere around the twenty-fourth she had put the hook over a husk's shoulder and pulled, and nothing had happened. She had simply stood there holding the pull with her arms shaking, and the husk had leaned against the thing closed over her and gone on leaning, until Katori came out of the doorway with her Ember still buttoned inside her coat and put a boot into the back of the husk's knee and it went down.
cues.reason: Contrasts Callie's physical failure with Katori's calm competence.

cues.delivery: Observational. Focus on the sensory details of cold and dew.
cues.from: Now the sky was going grey over the flats, and there was a lark somewhere, and the thing was still on her. The dew had come down in the night on every surface in the country except the clean dry shape of a girl sitting in a doorway. Her lips had split in two places. She had noticed that when she tried to lick them and her tongue stopped a finger's width short.
cues.through: Katori was sitting on the other side of the doorway with her knees up and her cap pulled down. She had not slept either. Callie was sure of it this time.
cues.reason: Sets the scene for Katori's confession.

cues.delivery: Flat, factual delivery. No emotional spikes on 'Twin-kindled'. Katori speaks as if stating a weather report.
cues.through: "There's a word for it," said Katori. "Old women use it. I've heard it said maybe twice in my life, and both times it was said the way you'd talk about a calf with two heads. Twin-kindled. That's all it means. Two doors at once, at the start, from two different places. I've never met one. I don't know anybody who has." She pulled her cap down another half inch. "So I'm not going to tell you what it means, because I don't know. I'm not going to tell you it's rare, because rare is a word for things people have counted, and nobody's counted this. I'm going to tell you I was wrong, and I'm sorry, and that you're going to have to work some of this out with me instead of from me."
cues.reason: The revelation is delivered with restraint; the weight comes from the facts.

cues.delivery: Callie's voice is small and analytical. She describes the 'yoke' mechanism with physical clarity.
cues.from: Callie sat with that for a while.
cues.through: "The barrow. On the way south. I had the strapping crossed over here." Callie lifted a hand that she could not feel and drew two lines across her own chest, over her coat, over the air a finger off her coat. "Four hundred miles. And when the horse kicked, it was like somebody got in on the other side of the yoke and pulled with me. And we've been pulling ever since. Both of us. All night." She stopped. "I've never stopped. I've never set it down."
cues.reason: Clarifies the mechanics of her power without magical flourish.

cues.delivery: Mechanical and deliberate. Emphasize the physical actions of strapping on the barrow.
cues.from: Katori said nothing for so long that Callie thought she hadn't understood.
cues.through: She backed into the barrow the way she had backed into it every morning since the spring. She lifted the strapping and brought it over her shoulders and crossed it over her chest. The webbing lay a finger's width off her coat all the way round, on the air, where the Ward was. She reached behind her for the buckle, and got it, and it took her a long time with hands she could not feel.
cues.reason: The solution is a physical act, not a spell.

cues.delivery: Slow pacing on the 'click' and the weight transfer. The sensation of relief should be physical.
cues.through: Then she reached behind her for the buckle, and unclipped it, and stepped out.
cues.reason: The climax of the barrow sequence is a release of tension.

cues.delivery: Quiet awe. The physical sensation of cold and touch is paramount.
cues.from: The first thing she felt was the air.
cues.through: "I couldn't have told you that," said Katori. "I want you to hear me say it. I could never have told you that. I'd have been at it with you for a week and I'd never have thought of the barrow."
cues.reason: Contrast the numbness with the sudden return of feeling.

cues.delivery: Mother's voice is weary but authoritative. Callie's drinking should feel desperate.
cues.from: Her mother was awake. Of course she was.
cues.through: "I know you don't. I'd prefer you not to be sick anyway. Otto's already done it once and I'd rather not start a fashion."
cues.reason: Re-establishes the mother-daughter bond and physical reality.

cues.delivery: Katori's explanation of ash is dry and functional. No wonder.
cues.from: Katori came back with a tin.
cues.through: "No," Katori agreed. "Nobody who lifts it does, mostly. I didn't, until I was thirteen and four months." She tipped the tin and let a little of the ash fall into the tin cup, into the last of the water. It went down through it slowly, turning, the way flour goes down through water, and it did not cloud it. The water went on being clear. "You emptied yourself last night. All the way down. What you've got in you, what comes through the door, fills up again on its own, slowly. It takes days. This fills it faster. That's all it does. That's all it's ever done. It's why a man with a door will pay you three times what a weighmaster will."
cues.reason: Ash is currency and fuel, not magic.

cues.delivery: Callie's reaction to the ash is subtle. Katori's command to sleep is firm.
cues.through: "They won't. You're dark." Katori stood. "You're as dark as Ines. Nothing out there can feel you any more than it can feel a stone. Go to sleep, Callie. That's not advice. That's the next part of the job."
cues.reason: The 'damp' sensation must be felt internally.

cues.delivery: Transition to afternoon. Pell's dialogue is dry and matter-of-fact.
cues.through: "Good. It's an improvement." He nodded toward the road. "They're back."
cues.reason: Grounds the scene in logistics after the emotional release.

cues.delivery: Ines's counting is precise. Pell's ledger reading is factual.
cues.from: Katori and Ines were coming up the gravel from the head of the causeway. They were walking slowly, the way people walk who have been on their knees for hours. Each of them had a canvas sack over one shoulder, and the sacks had the particular heavy, soft sag that Callie had only ever seen in a weighmaster's back room.
cues.through: "Your tenth," said Pell, and moved the pencil across one column and said a smaller number. It was still more than the jar, many times over. He turned the book round so she could see it written. "That's yours. That's in the book. Nobody at any wall between here and Meridian will be able to say it isn't."
cues.reason: The ash count validates Callie's value without fanfare.

cues.delivery: Callie's interaction with Duchess is tense but quiet. Otto's reassurance is earnest.
cues.from: Callie looked at the number in the small neat hand. She thought of the gate, and the columns, and a woman in a wagon who could not braid her own hair.
cues.through: Duchess watched them the whole time.
cues.reason: The horse's hostility adds a layer of unresolved tension.

cues.delivery: Callie's internal search is quiet. Katori's explanation of 'empty' vs 'gone' is technical.
cues.from: At dusk Callie tried to find the doors.
cues.through: "I don't know how. I watched you get it off this morning with a barrow, and I didn't know how then either." Katori's mouth moved very slightly. "So we'll find out together. You and me. And you'll teach me, some of it, because you're the only one who's been inside it."
cues.reason: Clarifies the nature of her power depletion.

cues.delivery: Callie's resolve is quiet. Katori's final line sets the next crisis.
cues.from: Callie turned the hook over in her hands. The tape on the cross was coming unwound at one end. She would have to fix that.
cues.through: "That," said Katori, "is what Pell was going to ask you at supper."
cues.reason: Ends on a logistical problem rather than an emotional one.

pauses.reason: Completed thought after Callie's realization of emptiness.
Emphasis on Katori's metaphor for Callie's feat.
